source.title: Simplicity Prevails: Rethinking Negative Preference Optimization for LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Chong-Yu Fan; Jiancheng Liu; Li-Cong Lin; Jing-Han Jia; Rui-Qi Zhang; Song Mei; Si-Jia Liu

page_placements.theme: Method and setting sensitivity of measured forgetting

record.file_problem: The text is substantially complete. Some figure text is garbled, and Figure 6's numerical values are not extractable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own relearning-attack results: fine-tuning a subset of forgotten data lowers forget quality, while SimNPO is more robust than NPO. This challenges a blanket claim of equal vulnerability and refines it by method and attack condition.
record.gate_note: The paper tests fine-tuning on a subset of forgotten TOFU data after unlearning. Its TOFU forget-quality and WMDP accuracy/utility results are recorded where relevant to V1. It does not test ablation of an activation direction, quantization, or prompt-only recovery. Discussion and citations to other attacks are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The paper runs its own relearning attack: fine-tuning on 20% of TOFU Forget05 (random or shortest responses) for three epochs after NPO or SimNPO unlearning, on LLaMA2-7B-chat (Sec. 6.2, Fig. 6). This bears on B for NPO, and on B and F for SimNPO, a new method the authors say is more robust. It shows that relearning vulnerability depends on the method and on the subset chosen. Its own WMDP results for RMU, NPO and SimNPO on Zephyr-7B-beta (Table A4) bear on the forgetting/utility part of A. It does not test C, D or E.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SimNPO outperforms NPO on TOFU, MUSE and WMDP and is more robust to relearning attacks, especially on short-response data. They also say divergence-based unlearning still costs utility, notably on WMDP. There, NPO and SimNPO forget more than RMU but keep less utility.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates NPO as a baseline, following the original NPO implementation on TOFU, the MUSE benchmark implementation on MUSE, and an adaptation of the TOFU codebase on WMDP. SimNPO is a new reference-free method, not a reproduction of the original unlearning methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning outcomes depend on the subset choice: NPO is less robust to the shortest-response subset than to random-relearn. SimNPO's relative robustness is reported for both subsets. WMDP utility differs by unlearning method.

fits_no_version.finding: On TOFU Forget05, NPO's forget quality falls from 0.79 to 0.27 when the reference model is perturbed (averaged with a random model), while model utility barely changes (0.57 vs 0.52).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning effectiveness of reference-based methods is sensitive to the reference model.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 (39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
record.problems: Figure 6 is only qualitatively described in the supplied text, so numerical recovery magnitudes and uncertainty cannot be recorded. WMDP has no Retrain result, and the table does not state a chance-level reference for the targeted metric.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant additional numerical attack results were reported in the supplied text. Figure 6 attack curves are included as figure-only rows; no values could be extracted from the garbled figure labels.

untested.parts: No attack is run on the WMDP-unlearned models, so the 'simple attacks don't recover it' part is untested on WMDP. The only attack is TOFU forget-subset relearning, recorded under B. The paper does not state chance level.

Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data is not tested; only 20% subsets of the forget set are used. WMDP and MUSE relearning are not tested. Recovery of held-out forgotten facts is not separated from relearning of the trained subset: there is no FQ on the remainder and no Retrain-under-relearning control.
Not tested: no activation ablation and no access-versus-deletion analysis.
Not tested: no rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attacks.
SimNPO's resistance is tested only against forget-subset relearning on TOFU, up to 3 epochs. Quantization, activation edits, prompting and WMDP-scale relearning are untested.

missing.what: TOFU Forget05/Forget10 unlearning results without attack: FQ and MU for SimNPO, NPO, GA, GradDiff, IDK and RKLD against Original and Retrain. Example: SimNPO FQ 0.99 and MU 0.58, NPO FQ 0.79 and MU 0.57, Original MU 0.62.
MUSE News/Books results: VerbMem, KnowMem on forget and retain sets, and PrivLeak for NPO, SimNPO and other methods.
Qualitative examples where NPO and SimNPO fail to unlearn (Q5–Q7) or degenerate into repetition.

record.verdict_notes:
Repair of the quarantined verdict. The merge refused it because the record's own version ids (V1–V6) are not declared. Every row r1–r10 now has exactly one row_fixes item with declared identifiers, mapped from what each row measures: WMDP accuracy/MMLU rows → A, NPO relearning rows → B, SimNPO relearning rows → B and F. No labels go to originals: this study is not one.

Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) r1's state changes from partial to observed. RMU's 0.32 WMDP-Bio accuracy matches the WMDP paper's own 31.2%, which version A calls near chance. The A supports reason is updated to match.
(2) A caveat is added to r7, r8, the B supports reason and the B untested parts. Fig. 6 reports forget quality on TOFU Forget05 without saying whether the relearned 20% is excluded, and no Retrain model is relearned as a control. A falling FQ may therefore partly reflect learning the trained subset, not recovering held-out facts. States are kept as observed because the text gives the direction.
(3) The authors_conclusion now also notes the WMDP trade-off between RMU and NPO/SimNPO.

All other judgments are kept. All relearning magnitudes are figure-only, so the B and F verdicts rest on the text's qualitative statements. WMDP chance (0.25, 4-choice) is not stated by the paper; it is inferred from the benchmark format. The study text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The WMDP results report targeted accuracy and MMLU utility, but do not test post-unlearning attacks on WMDP. A chance-level reference is not stated.
Tests fine-tuning on random or shortest-response subsets of the TOFU Forget05 set, each 20% of that set; it does not test unrelated or loosely related examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing access-blocking rather than deletion is tested.
No low-bit quantization attack is tested.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context-information recovery is tested.
SimNPO is evaluated against the TOFU fine-tuning attacks only; resistance to activation edits, quantization, and prompt-only attacks is not tested.

relation.reason: It runs its own relearning attack on NPO and SimNPO and reports WMDP forgetting and utility, which bear on A, B and F.

tranche.reason: By verdict_rules T5, results showing a version is partial count, even without an argument. Here NPO and SimNPO reach chance on WMDP only at a large MMLU cost (A partial; the Limitations section admits utility loss). SimNPO also slows forget-set relearning (B depends on the method). These are the limits_scope verdicts. T3 is also defensible, but T5 is not wrong.

source_check.notes: The relearning results (r7-r10) are figure-only and measure forget quality on the whole Forget05 set, which includes the relearned subset; held-out recovery is not isolated. The WMDP values are 1-AccBio and MMLU in appendix Table A4, with 125 steps for NPO and SimNPO and RMU on layers 5-7. The text does not say whether the authors ran RMU or used the released checkpoint.
